en.title: Kevin Feige Kept Scarlet Witch Out of VisionQuest for a Surprising Reason
en.summary: Marvel Studios head Kevin Feige actively prevented Wanda Maximoff's return in the Disney+ series VisionQuest. His reasoning? To let Vision's story stand entirely on its own.
en.body:
Fans eagerly awaiting a full Maximoff family reunion in **VisionQuest** were left with a bittersweet ending. While **Vision** (Paul Bettany) found a measure of peace and reunited with his sons, **Billy** and **Tommy Maximoff**, their mother, **Wanda Maximoff** (Elizabeth Olsen), remained absent, presumed lost after the events of *Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness*. However, it turns out this absence wasn't an oversight but a deliberate choice, orchestrated by none other than Marvel Studios president **Kevin Feige**.

Feige, according to series star and executive producer **Paul Bettany**, was adamant that Wanda should not appear in **VisionQuest**. His primary concern was preserving the show's narrative focus. Bettany revealed in an interview with The Playlist that Feige believed Wanda's presence would inevitably pull the story back into the orbit of **WandaVision**, overshadowing **Vision**'s own journey. The mandate was clear: **VisionQuest** needed to be its own entity, a story that could succeed and resonate independently.

> "There were questions about it, whether that should happen," Bettany explained. "Whether it opened up too much for the MCU, whether they wanted to do it later. I don’t know. But I remember having this conversation with [Kevin], and he said, ‘You and [series creator Terry Matalas] have done such a great job at making me care about Vision. I really don’t think you should distract from that by giving the audience that at the end of the [show]. It will just fundamentally all become about WandaVision again, and this should and can stand on its own.’"

This decision, while perhaps disappointing for those hoping for a complete familial reconciliation, speaks volumes about Feige's commitment to character development and the distinct storytelling potential of individual MCU projects. It underscores a desire to allow characters like Vision the space to forge their own paths and narratives, free from the gravitational pull of more established or fan-favorite storylines.

## The Fan Reaction and the Bigger Picture

The absence of **Scarlet Witch** was indeed a point of discussion among fans. Many hoped the series finale would offer closure for the Maximoff family, bringing **Vision**, **Wanda**, and their sons together. The post-credits scene, revealing **Doctor Doom** rescuing a weakened **Wanda** from Mount Wundagore, certainly provided a tantalizing hint of future possibilities and a connection to other major MCU players. However, Feige's strategic move prioritized the immediate narrative of **VisionQuest**, ensuring that the show’s emotional core remained firmly rooted in **Vision**’s evolution and his relationships with his children, rather than becoming a mere epilogue to **WandaVision**.

## What Lies Ahead for the Scarlet Witch

While **Wanda Maximoff** was kept out of **VisionQuest** to let **Vision** shine, her own story is far from over. The revelation that **Doctor Doom** has found her and intends to harness her power sets the stage for significant future developments. The exact nature of their relationship and how **Wanda** will navigate this new predicament remain to be seen, but her re-emergence is a certainty. Fans will undoubtedly be watching closely for any news regarding her next appearance, likely in a project that will allow her immense power and complex character arc to be explored further, perhaps even in direct confrontation with **Doctor Doom** himself.

content_raw: Spoilers for the VisionQuest finale.  VisionQuest has put a bow on Marvel Studios’ WandaVision trilogy , culminating in a nice, big group hug between the newly revitalized Vision (Paul Bettany) and his two magic sons, Tommy (Ruaridh Mollica) and Billy Maximoff (Joe Locke). Yet, some fans were disappointed that the Disney+ series didn’t close with a family reunion complete with Wanda Maximoff (Elizabeth Olsen), the former Avenger and sorceress who remained—just before the credits rolled on the VisionQuest finale anyway—under the ruins of Mount Wundagore, where she apparently perished after the events of Doctor Strange In The Multiverse Of Madness . Well, those fans can blame Marvel Studios head Kevin Feige for keeping Wanda out of VisionQuest —as it turns out, Marvel had bigger plans for the Scarlet Witch beyond merely smooshing the cheeks of her adoring sons. With Avengers: Doomsday looming, the superhero franchise doesn’t seem to have time for such mush.  In a new interview with The Playlist , VisionQuest star and executive producer Paul Bettany said Feige politely suggested Wanda stay away from the show so VisionQuest could stand apart from the series that spawned it. “There were questions about it, whether that should happen,” Bettany said. “Whether it opened up too much for the MCU, whether they wanted to do it later. I don’t know. But I remember having this conversation with [Kevin], and he said, ‘You and [series creator Terry Matalas] have done such a great job at making me care about Vision. I really don’t think you should distract from that by giving the audience that at the end of the [show]. It will just fundamentally all become about WandaVision again, and this should and can stand on its own.’ And I think he was right.” Setting aside the suggestion that VisionQuest ‘s should stand apart from WandaVision —Marvel promoted it as a trilogy capper, so it’s questionable whether anyone really thought it was supposed to—Olsen still appears in the sequel series. Scarlet Witch appears in shots taken from WandaVision to emotionally connect the two series, and, bewilderingly, a post-credits sequence following the series finale shows her being seemingly resurrected by Doctor Doom (Robert Downey Jr.), with the villain saying, “Your power will be mine,” which bodes ill for any Maximoff family reunion down the line.
